report.source_text: Two sets of blood cultures were sent from the emergency room, with samples obtained from right antecubital venepuncture and cuffed tunnelled haemodialysis catheter in the right IJV. One set of blood cultures was sent within 6 hours of admission during the haemodialysis session with samples from the haemodialysis circuit. These sets included one aerobic (BD Bactec Plus Aerobic/F medium) and one anaerobic bottle (BD BACTEC Lytic Anaerobic medium) each and were analysed using the Bactec FX 200 Automated Blood Culture System at 36°C and were negative for aerobes, anaerobes and yeasts after 2 and 7 days of incubation.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Metastatic methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection with infective endocarditis, pulmonary septic emboli, axillary abscess with a subacute presentation in a patient with chronic end-stage kidney disease on maintenance haemodialysis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A male patient in his 40s with end-stage diabetic nephropathy on maintenance haemodialysis presented with a 3-week history of intermittent, low to moderate-grade fever, generalized weakness, night sweats, exertional breathlessness, mild intermittent cough, loss of appetite, and left axillary pain for 2 days. Initial blood cultures were negative. Ultrasonography of the left axilla on the fourth day of admission revealed a small collection, which was aspirated. Microscopy of the aspirate showed gram-positive bacteria, and subsequent culture identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). A chest CT with contrast showed left loculated hydropneumothorax with multiple cavitary nodules and some nodules with reverse halo signs, consistent with pulmonary septic emboli. Transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography revealed multiple tiny vegetations at the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve with near moderate tricuspid regurgitation, confirming infective endocarditis.
